cards.text: Last time, the Sanhedrin got so heated that the Roman commander had to pull Paul out by force. The following night the Lord stood near Paul, told him to take courage, and said he must also testify in Rome. When daylight comes, though, the Jews form a conspiracy against him.

cards.question: The plotters bind themselves with an oath. What do they swear not to do until Paul is dead?
How big is this oath-swearing crew? More than ___ men are in on the plot against Paul.

cards.text: More than forty grown men, no food, no drink, until the job's done, and they take that oath straight to the chief priests and elders. Friend, I skip ONE cookie break and the whole bakery hears about it.

cards.question: The plotters ask the chief priests and the Sanhedrin for one favor. What is it?

answers.text: Ask the commander to bring Paul down
Ask the commander to set Paul free
Ask the governor to hear Paul's case

cards.question: The plotters want the request for Paul to look like the Sanhedrin just needs to examine his case more carefully.
If the commander goes along with the request, where do the plotters plan to kill Paul?

cards.text: More than forty men, a solemn oath, a whole secret plan. And the one who hears about it? The son of Paul's sister. Of ALL the people in Jerusalem!

cards.question: Paul's nephew now knows about the plot. What does he do?

answers.text: Goes into the barracks and tells Paul
Goes to the chief priests and pleads

cards.text: Paul gets the news, and he doesn't sit on it. He calls over one of the centurions.

cards.question: Paul tells the centurion to take the young man to the ___, because he has something to tell him.

cards.text: The centurion brings him in, and the commander takes the young man by the hand and draws him aside to ask what he needs to say. That's a boss who actually LISTENS.

cards.question: Paul's nephew says the Jews will ask the commander to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin. When?
Paul's nephew tells the commander it's fine to go along with the Sanhedrin's request.

cards.text: He lays it all out: more than forty men ready to ambush Paul, just waiting on the commander's yes. So the commander sends the young man off with one instruction.

cards.question: What does the commander tell Paul's nephew before he goes?

answers.text: Don't tell anyone you reported this
Come back if you hear anything more
Go warn Paul's friends in the city

cards.text: The commander doesn't wait around. He calls two of his centurions and starts giving orders.

cards.question: The commander sends Paul off with only a handful of guards.

cards.text: More than forty men plan an ambush, and the commander answers with two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen: FOUR HUNDRED SEVENTY. That's not an escort, that's a STADIUM letting out.

cards.question: The commander orders the whole escort to go to ___.
The commander has the escort leave Jerusalem in broad daylight.

cards.text: They head out in the third hour of the night, and the commander even provides mounts to get Paul there safely. A prisoner with an armed escort AND a ride? Friend, that's a VIP car service.

cards.question: Paul is being taken safely to someone important in Caesarea. Who?

cards.text: The commander also writes a letter to Felix, the governor, to go along with Paul. And the letter finally gives us the commander's name: Claudius Lysias.

cards.question: In his letter, Lysias says he came with his troops and rescued Paul. Why does he say he stepped in?

answers.text: He had learned Paul was a Roman citizen
He had heard Paul was a known prophet
He had been ordered by the governor

cards.text: Funny thing: back in Acts 22:29, Lysias only realized Paul was a citizen after he'd put him in chains, so this letter tells it a LITTLE nicer. Hey, I do the same thing every time I tell the story of my first batch.

cards.question: Lysias writes that he took Paul to the Sanhedrin to understand the charges. What did the accusation turn out to be about?
Lysias writes that Paul deserves death or prison.
Lysias ends the letter by telling Felix about the plot, and says he's told Paul's accusers to make their case in front of Felix.

cards.text: The soldiers follow their orders and bring Paul by night to Antipatris. So far, so good.

cards.question: The next day, the soldiers head back to the barracks. Who goes on with Paul from Antipatris?

cards.text: The horsemen ride into Caesarea, hand Felix the letter and present Paul to him. Felix reads it and asks one question: what province is Paul from?

cards.question: Felix learns that Paul is from the province of ___.
So what does Governor Felix decide to do with Paul?

answers.text: Hear his case when the accusers arrive
Send him back to Jerusalem right away
Set him free since there's no charge

cards.text: Until then, Paul is kept under guard in Herod's Praetorium. Hang on to your apron, friend, because there's a whole lot more of Paul's story coming.
